author: Jurij
text:
Hello everyone,

what a beatiful place you have built here.

I'm deeply thankful and honored to be given this opportunity to learn from the very best traders around.

Took me a long time to find my way here. I started trading around 3
years ago as a price action trader (market structure, candle PA like pin
 bars. etc...) then immersed in the world of S/D trading (Sam Seiden)
where I gained a new understanding of the market.

But there was (or better still is) always a missing piece to truly
understand the market. Sure, winning 38% of the times while trading S/D
zones (TP 3R) let's you gain some pips but it is still a pain when you
get the so often losing streak of 5-9 trades.

I always knew that there was somewhere a better place to learn the mechanics of the markets,

something that describes and show how everything works, in all time
frames and where B.S. like "noise" is a fancy word for incompetence

I don't believe in self-limits.

Your perception becomes your reality.

If you can think it, then you can achieve it.

How often do you hear, predicting the market is not possible.

Let alone the "it's all random" talk.

This will be my small corner where I'll share my thoughts, understandings, doubts, progress and of course trades.

Please feel always free to post any question, suggestion and criticism.

Learning and teaching is only possible through quality feedback.

Cya

Jurij

author: Jurij
text:
Thanks IF.

Yes, which level is going to hold, the only trading question that matters.

The journey for me to answer that question starts here and from the basics.

So let's begin

Disclaimer for this and all future posts: the following contents come
 from my own understanding of the original teachings by IF and other
members, so always be aware that I could be totally wrong and that each
unit of knowledge is subject to my own interpretation, filtering and may
 not reflect the original concepts as intended by IF

Caps on price

Every S/D trader knows them in and out, yet the best, strongest and perfect looking ones still fail.

I can conclude from my own experience that the shape of the base and
departure strength from a level have only limited influence on the
overall outcome.

What really matters, as RTM teaches, is the context.

But before I get into that. There are some important clues that I
consider to determine the quality of the base, I'm sure someone else
here at RTM pointed them out.

An interesting fact is that many traders think that consolidation (bases
 in RBD/RBD/RBR/DBD) means low activity (volume) and that momentum bars
happen due to high volume. Sure, sometimes this is right, but most of
the time momentum bars (liquidity gaps) are thin market moves (low
volume) because price has to move in one direction once the last
unfilled order is filled and ready to move to the next liquidity zone
(base), where enough opposing orders get filled to stop price for some
time, until again the balance gets broken one way or the other.

This is also the reason why price bounces from those bases, because of unfilled orders left over from the last battle.

S/D traders say that those orders at the bases are left there for undefined time, even for years.

But it was a real revelation to me what RTM teaches about targets (PAZ).

Another common reason for RBD/DBR failures is also explained by RTM.

Just by knowing this and the above, we should be able to filter out many losses.

Now to what really matters, the context where caps happen.

Target 1 was there because of the past history:

I see that in the last part I'm already ahead with FTRs, engulfs and targets.

I will try to get in those in my next series of posts.

And it is also clear from the above, that one concept taken in isolation
 (in this case price caps) is not enough to decipher price.

author: Jurij
text:
The more I immerse in the concepts (FTR, FL, engulf, PAZ) the more doubts arise.

There are moments where clearity emerges when I see them working
together, then everything makes sense and I feel relieved, but then the
next chart I open or after some hours, when I try to start again, all is
 gone, again, only confusion is left.

So I will continue to post my units of understanding to cement what I know.

And hopefully in case something is wrong there's at least a chance that someone might point it out.

FTR/FL

The FTR is where everything begins. In my opinion, the most crucial part of the puzzle.
